messages:
jess (support): Customer on Next.js edge reported intermittent 401s only in production builds after bundling. Dev server works fine. They sent a repro bundle + logs.
jess (support): summary: auth header present in dev, missing in prod bundle requests to api.redwood.example -> 401. Appears when app is bundled with Vite/esbuild for edge.
li (eng-runtime): do we have the customer's package.json exports/entries? likely picking wrong entry (cjs vs esm) or a shim being tree-shaken.
jess (support): pasted the minimal package.json they used:
```json
{
  "name": "my-app",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "dependencies": {
    "@redwood/inference": "^2.4.1"
  },
  "build": "vite build"
}
```
jess (support): their bundle report shows vite resolving @redwood/inference -> dist/esm/index.js for build, but runtime trace shows the bundled fetch wrapper using a fallback that doesn't forward Authorization in edge context.
tom (eng): can you paste the SDK package.json exports/types block from their installed node_modules (or the SDK's published package)? sometimes conditional exports + types leads bundlers to prefer the CJS runtime shim.
jess (support): yes, pasted from node_modules/@redwood/inference/package.json:
```json
"exports": {
  ".": {
    "import": "./dist/esm/index.js",
    "require": "./dist/cjs/index.js",
    "types": "./dist/index.d.ts"
  },
  "./package.json": "./package.json"
}
```
li (eng-runtime): aha — the exports map includes a scalar "types" under the main export which is nonstandard placement (types should be top-level field), some bundlers ignore it and pick the require path or a runtime shim. If the bundle ends up using the CJS shim that wraps fetch differently, headers can get lost in edge builds.
maria (devex): customer also showed tsconfig + bundler: TS 5.3, Vite 4, target es2022. Using pnpm with node 20. Repro steps they sent:
```bash
npx create-next-app --edge
pnpm install
pnpm build
pnpm start
# curl to edge route that proxies to /v1/generate
```
jess (support): logs from prod bundle: will paste portion — note request to our API missing Authorization header, server logs show "missing api key".
li (eng-runtime): quick local check: if you bundle and the package selected is CJS runtime, the SDK's node-only auth shim tries to set headers via internal client which is compiled away in edge and ends up using global fetch without proper header merge. Not ideal.
tom (eng): proposed fixes: (1) publish a package.json with "types" at top-level and move exports to explicit subpaths ("./package.json" + "./*"), (2) add an "import"-first ESM-only entry with no CJS fallback for edge environments, (3) add a short note in docs about bundlers and Next.js edge.
li (eng-runtime): quick patch I can cut: make the ESM entry the default export (keep require key for old users), and add a tiny runtime guard so fetch wrapper always preserves existing headers in edge (merge Authorization if present). Also add a test that simulates Vite static analysis picking the wrong entry.
maria (devex): also we should add a troubleshooting snippet for support: commands to dump resolved package entry during build:
```bash
node -e "console.log(require.resolve('@redwood/inference'))"
# and for ESM build:
node -p "import.meta.resolve('@redwood/inference')"
```
jess (support): customer asked for a temporary workaround they can apply now — what to tell them?
tom (eng): advise rollback to SDK v2.3.x (where packaging different) OR force Vite to prefer esm via alias in vite.config:
```js
resolve: {
  alias: {
    '@redwood/inference': path.resolve(__dirname, 'node_modules/@redwood/inference/dist/esm/index.js')
  }
}
```
li (eng-runtime): that's fine as a stopgap. I'll prepare the release patch (v2.4.2) that reworks exports + types and adds header-merge guard. I'll also add a unit to prevent regressions with bundlers.
deploy-bot: release v2.4.2 branch created by li/eng-runtime -- will run CI. :rocket:
tom (eng): assign follow-up: add docs blurb about exports map + bundler quirks and a FAQ entry for "401 only in production bundle".
jess (support): sending customer the workaround + ETA for patch (2 business days). thanks all. :white_check_mark:
